summary: Phase 149O.20G -- HMIC v1.2 HBDC 25-File / 5-Contract Production Identity Alignment Independent Verification: INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION VERIFICATION ONLY, zero src/pcae/**, scripts/**, or contract files modified. Initial inspection confirmed repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, pcae health/check/status-coherence/push-check/runtime-inspect/notify-status all as expected, 149O.20F confirmed completed/pushed via pcae phase-report show --latest and pcae phase-report reconcile --phase-id 149O.20F (status: reconciled, mutation: none). Read HMIC-001 (HMIC-REQ-050/052-053/067-069/145 directly), the 149O.20E/20F phase documents, and the production certification/cutover/admin source files. Independently, freshly extracted the live contract target via regex over the raw HMIC-001 contract text (never importing production's own constants as the oracle): HMIC-REQ-050's fenced enumeration is exactly 25 entries; HMIC-REQ-067's contract_versions is exactly 5 members {HMRC-001, HATP-001, HSCE-001, RAE-001, HBDC-001}. Independently, freshly extracted current production via regex over the module's own source text (cross-checked against the actually-imported tuples, ruling out a stale-bytecode mismatch): _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES exactly 25, _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES exactly 5. Confirmed exact dual equality -- both sets equal by content AND by literal presentation order, zero extras/omissions/aliases. Reconstructed the pre-20F baseline via git show 43ecacb9 (149O.20F's own confirmed phase-entry commit): exactly 24 files / 4 contract members; exact delta = docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md / HBDC-001 in both dimensions, matching 149O.20D.1/149O.20E's named expected delta precisely; all 24/4 original entries confirmed a strict subset of the current 25/5. AST-diffed the entire 149O.20F production diff (43ecacb9..HEAD on src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py, the only production file touched): zero function/class bodies changed, confirmed via ast.dump comparison over every FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef node -- identical node sets, identical dumps. Wrote a from-scratch, independent reimplementation of the HMIC-REQ-054/056-058 two-level SHA-256 digest construction: golden-cross-checked exactly against production's own derive_implementation_scope_digest (identical hex digest, 7b9cbe2f...); confirmed 25/25 frozen files individually digest-sensitive via one-byte modeled mutations; confirmed the independently-reconstructed pre-20F 24-file digest differs from the current 25-file digest for an identical present-day snapshot. Built a disposable git-archive fixture (real working tree never mutated) and exercised production's own live derive_implementation_scope_digest/derive_contract_versions functions directly via subprocess: HBDC-001 same-version content mutation changes implementation_scope_digest but leaves contract_versions unchanged; a version-header bump changes derived contract_versions[HBDC-001] (and the digest, since content also changed); a malformed Contract-ID raises ContractIdentityDerivationError (fail-closed) -- explicit, independent dual-binding proof, both dimensions demonstrated material, not inferred from tuple membership alone. Confirmed the other four pre-existing bound contracts' own dual binding remains unweakened (each individually mutated in the same fixture, each still changes the digest). Confirmed HBDC missing/symlinked/non-regular-file all fail closed against production's real _resolve_and_reject_unsafe_frozen_file safety checks (FrozenFileDerivationError in all three cases). Confirmed core self-binding: mutating hatp_mandatory_certification.py's own post-edit bytes inside the fixture changes the digest; restoring the bytes returns the digest exactly to baseline -- current, not stale, source participates. Searched for and confirmed absence of any legacy-scope override signature, validation cache (lru_cache/@cache), module-level import-time derivation call, duplicate frozen path or contract ID, or caller-suppliable contract-identity/digest/version/count parameter on either derive_* function (inspect.signature confirms both take exactly (root)). AST-compared derive_implementation_scope_digest, derive_contract_versions, derive_implementation_commit, _validate_at_root, and the top-level certification validator: byte-identical dumps, phase entry vs. current. Confirmed scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py and hatp_mandatory_cutover.py byte-identical to phase entry via direct text comparison; confirmed the dynamic readiness-fact wiring 149O.20F itself found (correcting a stale hard-coded-False characterization) remains present, unredesigned. Independently reproduced 149O.20F's own before/after historical-repin claim using a disposable git worktree at the phase-entry commit (not git stash, to avoid disturbing the working tree during this read-mostly phase): the broad HMIC/HBDC sweep shows 37 failed/818 passed at phase entry vs. 33 failed/869 passed at HEAD (pre-20G-test-module) -- zero new failures, 15 fixed by 20F's repair, and one pre-existing residual (149O.20C's own stale v1.1-current-version assertion) confirmed to reproduce identically at phase entry, i.e. pre-existing and unrelated to both 20F and 20G. Modeled pre-20F 24/4, pre-repair-v1.2 24-file/5-member, and v1.1 24/4 certification replay attacks against current live production: all rejected via digest and/or contract-identity mismatch, no grandfathering. Called assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness read-only against the real host: ready=False; the mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified check itself reports ACCESS_ERROR (no repository-identity.json established) -- no state created by this read. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20G_HMIC_V1_2_HBDC_25_FILE_5_CONTRACT_PRODUCTION_IDENTITY_ALIGNMENT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md and one new, independent test module, tests/test_phase_149o_20g_hmic_v1_2_hbdc_25_file_5_contract_production_identity_alignment_independent_verification.py (40 tests, all passed, none importing 20F's own test module or constants as an oracle). Ran the broad HMIC/HBDC sweep (including the new module): 33 failed/909 passed/4 skipped/31041 deselected, zero new failures relative to the pre-20G-module baseline. Ran the repository-standard Fast Green suite (pytest -m fast_green -n auto): 59 failed, 6549 passed, 4 skipped, 1 collection error (raw) -- 1 pre-existing fido2-import collection error (matches 20F's own citation); 1 confirmed-spurious concurrent-task-lifecycle-state failure in test_backend_cli.py (a different node ID than 20F's own citation, consistent with xdist-order-dependent flake; confirmed 307/307 passing in isolation); the remaining 58 independently reproduced identically at phase-entry commit 43ecacb9 via two separate disposable git worktrees (covering the -k sweep's failing modules plus six additional Fast-Green-only modules not in that sweep) -- all 58 pre-existing, none attributable to 149O.20F or 149O.20G. Zero new regressions. Verdict: HMIC v1.2 HBDC 25-FILE / 5-CONTRACT PRODUCTION IDENTITY ALIGNMENT: INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- production exactly matches the verified HMIC v1.2 identity, HBDC dual binding complete. B-149O.20D-1: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT CONTRACT + PRODUCTION IDENTITY BOUNDARY (Class-B deployment/provisioning remains deferred). HBDC-BINDING-GATE: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT CONTRACT + PRODUCTION IDENTITY BOUNDARY -- CLASS-B DEPLOYMENT VERIFIER / ENVIRONMENT-LOCK IMPLEMENTATION PENDING (explicitly not equivalent to Class-B deployment verified). W-1 remains independently closed. B-149O.19.3-1 remains independently closed; its four provider/hardware files confirmed still present within the current 25-file target. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION/ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY -- DEPLOYMENT/OPERATIONAL ACTIVATION DEFERRED, no upgrade. Class-B remains CONTRACT VERIFIED -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize provisioning, certification, activation, or Class-B verifier/environment-lock implementation. Recommended next phase: a Class-B Deployment Verifier / Model-A Environment-Lock Implementation Architecture or Plan phase, addressing the retained non-blocking implementation-coverage gaps (effective ACL/group verification, full ancestor-chain verification, hard-link verification, Python environment-lock conformance) -- architecture/plan first, then isolated-mode implementation, then independent verification, before any real provisioning phase.
